claims.text: The initial AlCoCrFeNi alloy is a eutectic high-entropy alloy with a coarse dual-phase lamellar colony structure.
Internal boundaries in the coarse lamellar colonies serve as microcrack-initiation sites.
A trace Nb addition followed by isothermal aging will form Nb-rich nanoprecipitates.
The Nb-rich nanoprecipitates will form preferentially at lamellar-colony boundaries or interfaces.
Aging at approximately 600 °C for 3–5 hours will induce the proposed interfacial nanoprecipitation.
The nanoprecipitates will impede dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion will increase yield strength through precipitation hardening.
The nanoprecipitates will impede crack propagation by blunting or deflecting crack tips at lamellar interfaces.
Crack-tip blunting or deflection will mitigate microcrack initiation and coalescence.
Mitigating microcrack initiation and coalescence will increase room-temperature tensile ductility.
The Nb-added and aged alloy will have statistically significantly higher yield strength than the unmodified baseline.
The Nb-added and aged alloy will have statistically significantly higher uniform elongation at room temperature than the unmodified baseline.
The predicted strength and ductility improvements require an optimally controlled nanoprecipitate distribution.
Excessive, irregular, coarse, or unevenly distributed precipitates could embrittle the alloy or reduce its ductility.
The approach may be applicable to eutectic high-entropy alloys compositionally similar to AlCoCrFeNi.
The intervention may be ineffective when Nb concentration, aging temperature, or aging duration is not properly optimized.
